programmes.d: Joel McHale stars as Jack, a renowned adventure reporter for an outdoor magazine.
Clark, Emma, and Mason must intervene when Jack decides to try online dating and creates the worst profile ever for himself.
Jack faces the ultimate test of his survival skills when he's forced to crash at Clark's tiny apartment while he searches for a place of his own.
When Adam notices his Dad's increasingly forgetful behavior, he struggles with how to approach him to discuss it.
When Adam and Andi agree on a present-free Valentine's Day, Adam gives the gift he planned for Andi to his mother instead.
When Andi gets Bev (Swoosie Kurtz) a spot volunteering at the hospital, Joe becomes bored and starts spending too much time with Adam.
When the gang decides to take a trip to Vermont to check out the fall foliage, they find themselves wishing they had never left home. Meanwhile, Russell has renewed faith in his marriage to Liz.
Jeff uses an app to call Audrey's voicemail directly; a salesman backs Adam when his friends question his sartorial choices.

Audrey encourages Jeff to eat better after discovering he has high cholesterol, but Jeff starts sneaking out with Brenda for unhealthy food; Russell struggles to keep up with his new intern on the party circuit.
When Andi and Adam disagree about Kate attending a dance with an older boy, Adam tries to outsmart Andi to win the argument.
Adam attempts to organize a birthday dinner for Andi and he discovers that managing guests isn't easy.
When Adam and Andi lose footage of an intimate moment they accidentally recorded, they have to track it down before anyone can see it.

Jeff and Audrey engage in a battle of wills when she refuses toadmit that she hates the armchair she ordered, while Jeff pretends to love it. Meanwhile, Russell brings a sexual harassment suit against Timmy.
In order to convince Audrey he is making an effort in theirrelationship, Jeff sends her on a romantic scavenger hunt, with mixed results.
When Audrey thinks her maid needs help getting money to fix herlimp, she asks her neighbors to help contribute, only to find out she misunderstood what the maid needed the money for.
When Ray's "Zia Sarina" comes to visit all the way from Italy, he's thrilled finally to meet a relative whom the whole family likes.
When Debra gets depressed because Ray would rather eat his mother's cooking, Ray asks his mom to give Debra cooking lessons.
When Raymond takes over the family checkbook to prove to Debra "how easy it can be" to balance it, he nearly creates a financial disaster that sends the family to the poorhouse.
When Raymond goes on a citizen's ride-along in his brother's patrol car and sees Robert risk his life during a hold-up, he gains new respect for him.
When Ally, claiming that there are monsters in her room, insists on sleeping in her parents' bed, Ray and Debra do everything they can to slay the monsters so they can get a good night's sleep.
Debra discovers that her mother-in-law, Marie, likes Robert's girlfriend, Amy, better than she likes her because Amy is a "good girl."
Debra brings an "unapproved snack" to Ally's T-Ball game and Ray doesn't stand up for her -- prominently displaying his fear of being disliked.
When Robert's traffic school students complain that his class causes severe insomnia, he practices on members of his family -- who turn out to be even tougher critics.
Debra tries to teach Raymond how to have a "normal" mid-life crisis like everyone else, after he starts planning for his burial.
When Debra gives away all the "baby stuff" at a family garage sale, Ray gets upset that she doesn't want to have any more children.
After Raymond asks Debra why she ever married him, they take a walk back in time -- to the very beginning of it all, in Part One of a special two-part episode.
Ray fears that Debra is more interested in the wedding than in him, in the conclusion of a special two-part episode.
When Ray's house is tented for termites, he moves his entire family into his parents' house and gives Frank and Marie a taste of their own medicine, on the third season premiere.
After Frank has one accident too many, Debra decides that the kids can't ride with him anymore, which makes Raymond realize that his dad is getting older.
Upset because she thinks the kids like their new babysitter, Lisa, better than their mommy, Debra makes a desperate choice -- she asks Marie to step in.
After Raymond embarrasses Debra at Ally's school auction, she hints that she's going to "get him back" and Ray lives in fear of her retribution.
When Debra's mother comes to visit the family for a week, Debra finds herself shocked to discover that she wishes her own mom were more like Marie.
Joel McHale stars as Jack, a renowned adventure reporter for an outdoor magazine.
Clark, Emma, and Mason must intervene when Jack decides to try online dating and creates the worst profile ever for himself.
Jack faces the ultimate test of his survival skills when he's forced to crash at Clark's tiny apartment while he searches for a place of his own.
The Millennials discover a huge secret about Jack's love life when they clean out his decades-old storage unit.
Human Resources forbids Jack from giving his staff any feedback at all after he crushes Clark with a brutally honest performance review.
When Emma quits after being turned down for a raise, Jack and Roland become the magazine's newest and worst ever social media managers.
Jack tests the Millennials' survival skills when he takes them camping for the first time and leaves them alone in the woods without their smartphones.
Jack desperately begs his co-workers to pretend to be his closest friends at a dinner party after his lack of an inner circle begins to concern his girlfriend, Rachel.
When Jack fixates on his relationship with Rachel to the detriment of the magazine and his friends, Eddie and Roland try to break him of his obsession habit.
When Jack can't concentrate because of the millennials' distracting juvenile behavior, Brooke installs cubicles in the bullpen.
When Jack insults Ricky (Rory Scovel), the magazine's I.T. manager, the "techspert" exacts his revenge by leaking office emails that cause the staff to turn on each other.
Jack gets caught up in Roland and Brooke's family drama when they both enlist his help to keep bombshells about their love lives from each other.
At the magazine's notoriously carnal company retreat, feelings resurface between Jack and Brooke as they work together to help Clark finally hook up with Emma
